case.caveats: Same five-primer AMOS cocktail. Here the productive orientation is the reverse of the B. ovis and B. suis cases: the B. melitensis-specific primer is the forward primer and the IS711 primer is the reverse. Measured in silico as 733 bp at 1209132..1209864 on AE008917.1, i.e. 2 bp above the paper's gel estimate of 731 bp - agarose-gel resolution, not a mismatch, since strain 16M is the exact strain the paper tested. Useful precisely because the expected value is gel-derived and therefore genuinely independent of the template sequence. The IS711 primer matches 5 sites on AE008917.1; only one pairs with the B. melitensis primer.
case.citation: Bricker BJ, Halling SM. Differentiation of Brucella abortus bv. 1, 2, and 4, Brucella melitensis, Brucella ovis, and Brucella suis bv. 1 by PCR. J Clin Microbiol. 1994;32(11):2660-2666. doi:10.1128/jcm.32.11.2660-2666.1994. PMID 7852552.
case.loci_justification: AMOS-PCR is run at the bench as a five-primer multiplex; the pair scored here is the species-specific pair for this template, and the IS711 copy it reports is a single chromosomal locus. Filed under the 'irap-remap' panel for convenience, which is a label and not a statement about locus multiplicity.
